newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KFC plans to triple meat production.
newsitem.headline: KFC plans to triple meat production.

text.p: Malaysian fast-food chain KFC Holdings (M) Bhd said on Thursday it plans to triple its production of ready-to-eat chicken products over the next three to five years.
"We want to increase our production by three times over the next three to five years," said Foo Peng Peng, divisonal director of Ayamas Food Corp Bhd told Reuters.
Ayamas is a 67 percent owned subsidiary of KFC Holdings, which operates Southeast Asia's largest chain of KFC outlets.
"We want to expand, enlarge and deepen our presence in the ready-to-eat market," said Harris Beh, group executive director of KFC Holdings.
"We want to be the protein plate of Malaysia," he said after attending a fund managers' conference.

The officials said the cost of the expansion would be around 25 million ringgit of which five million would be spent on land acquisitions, 15 million on automation and five milion on tool-room facilities and salaries.
Ayamas currently processes 85,000 chickens per day. The firm already sells processed chicken meat including chicken burgers and bite-size chicken pieces.
